slides.title: The OB is only a location
slides.body: Bullish OB on NQ: the last down candle before the impulse, 24,396-24,404. It shows where buyers stepped in before. Not whether they are there today.

slides.title: Selling absorbed in the zone
slides.body: Price taps the OB and sellers hit the bid 3x or more the ask one tick above, three prices in a row. Yet the low barely moves: passive buyers absorb it all.

slides.title: The delta flip
slides.body: Next bar: buyers lift the ask 3x or more the bid one tick below, three prices in a row. Delta goes from -1,205 to +700. Now the zone has a witness.

slides.title: When the OB fails
slides.body: Sell imbalances keep printing, delta stays negative and price closes under 24,396. Nobody defended the zone. That's not an entry, it's your invalidation.
slides.tip: Close below the OB = it's gone.

caption:
Order blocks don't hold. BUYERS do. 🎯

An order block is a location: the last opposite candle before an impulse, where institutions stepped in before. It doesn't tell you whether anyone is still there today. The footprint does. Inside a bullish order block you want to see selling that gets absorbed: heavy prints on the bid, stacked sell imbalances, but no new low. Then the flip: buyers lift the ask with stacked buy imbalances and delta turns positive. If sell imbalances keep printing and price closes below the zone, it's not support anymore.

1️⃣ Order block = where to look, never the entry on its own
2️⃣ Heavy selling with no new low = passive buyers absorbing
3️⃣ Stacked buy imbalances + delta flip = the trigger
4️⃣ Close below the order block with negative delta = invalidation
